title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator circuit for fly walking
source_locator: Main text, section 'A separate class of descending neurons recruits an overlapping rhythm generating circuit'; Fig. 5c-e; Methods 'Optogenetics experiments with 3D joint kinematics'
quote: we optogenetically activated DNb08 neurons in decapitated flies and found that they reliably produced rhythmic leg movements
mapping_basis: Paper uses the MANC/Namiki type name DNb08; driver_lines.csv lists SS70620 as DNb08 only.
stimulation: 638 nm laser, 1200 Hz, 30% duty cycle, focused at front-left body-coxa joint; 5 s stim-on trials; intensity not stated for DNb08
sensory_condition: decapitated, de-winged, tethered; Fig. 5d schematic shows no treadmill; text says movements were more reliable with the treadmill removed
frequency_note: not reported; Fig. 5e reports a femur-tibia kinematic rhythmicity measure for left front and middle legs (stim on vs off)
coordination_notes: described as resembling searching movements, qualitatively different from coordinated walking
penetrance: front and middle leg rhythmicity higher in stim-on than stim-off trials (paired t-tests p = 0.036, 0.004)
n_flies_note: 8 stim-on and 4 stim-off trials per fly
notes: Hind legs are not reported in Fig. 5d-e or text. Surface inferred as air from the Fig. 5d schematic and text; not stated explicitly in Methods. Simulation rhythmicity results for DNb08 were seen in the same section (see sightings.csv); they were not used.

frequency_note: median ~7-8 Hz all legs read from Fig. 1e; not stated in text
coordination_notes: tripod-like coordination (TCS), left-right antiphase, ipsilateral adjacent legs antiphase (Fig. 3c-d)
notes: Control decapitated flies did not step. saw_simulation_score true because a Pugliese simulation driver call for DNg100 was seen (sightings.csv).
